newsitem.title: JORDAN: Bank of Jordan approves capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Jordan approves capital increase.

text.p: Bank of Jordan chairman Tawfiq al-Fakhouri said on Saturday the bank's shareholders approved plans to double its capital to 21 million dinars to meet Central Bank minimum capital requirements.
Fakhouri said the decision was taken at an extraordinary assembly of shareholders on Thursday.

He said half the increase would be covered by a transfer of cash from reserves and retained profit, translating into a bonus share issue to existing shareholders of one share for every two shares they own.
"We will issue a free half-share for every existing share, raising the capital by 5.25 million dinars," he told Reuters.
The remaining capital increase would be made through a sale of new shares, he said. The bank has not decided whether the share subscription would be a public or closed offering.
Fakhouri, who was involved in merger talks earlier this year with Jordan Kuwait Bank, said the majority of Jordan Kuwait shareholders were now opposed to the deal and it would not go through.
Jordan's Central Bank has been encouraging mergers between Jordan's smaller banks to create a leaner, healthier banking industry.
Banks which do not merge have been forced to find other ways of meeting the Central Bank's December 31 deadline for raising their paid-up capital to 20 million dinars.
Bank of Jordan posted 1996 net profits of 5.07 million dinars against 2.99 million dinars in 1995. Its assets stood at 534 million dinars against 457 million in 1995.
